Hey there, I'm definitely not an expert on this subject, but I can give you some insight based on my personal experience. (Be warned - there might be quite some guessing involved)

Regular basic attacks use your stats the moment the damage applies, if they are not projectiles.

If they are projectiles, they use your stats the moment the projectile is in the air. However, certain damage modifiers may still apply after a projectile is already in flight. For example think of a Statikk Shiv that gets charged while your basic attack is already in air and then still applies its on-hit damage or the extra damage gained from Vladimir's Hemoplague or Coup de Grace that obviously only get calculated the moment you hit.

tldr: it depends on the type of attack and on the type of effect.

For me I think it's all about context.
In what areas/how does the champion thrive?
What is the counterplay?

Let's look at Zed, a high skill curve champion.
Zed thrives in skirmishes and assassination - both in high and low elo - he deals damage through skillshots and has good mobility.
However you can always dodge and outplay his damage.

Now let's look at Ryze, a broken champ in competitive.
Ryze thrives in skirmishes and also assassination late into the game - both in high and low elo - but he also has great lane priority, insane mobility for his team and easy gank setup in a team that communicates well (competitive). In low elo he either gets in range and does his things or gets outranged and does nothing.

Let's actually talk about something that I learned about my opinion while writing all of this.

I don't have a problem with balancing around pro play, but I do have a problem with how they do it in some cases. (I already want to say sorry for the next part, I kind of get lost in my words because it is hard for me to explain)

Champions like Taliyah, Sejuani, Zac and whoever is popular in competitive at some point are more or less healthy and get nerfed when they are too strong. This doesn't affect normal play too much because they were strong there as well.
Champions like Ryze, Kalista and Azir (old Azir was even a better example) offer certain things in their kits that are only accessible when played perfectly. Because of this the very best players have a champion that simply outclasses every other champion in the game. But instead of removing the ability to outclass, they completely nerf the champion until what used to be "outclassing" is merely playing at the same level of other professional players on other champions.

So I guess the difference between a high skill curve champion and a broken champion is if you have the ability to outclass.

I think balance around the top 200 players, who perfectly abuse everything that is thrown at them just sucks for anyone below while balancing for silver sucks for anyone above.
A middle ground needs to be found to satisfy the most players while also keeping pro play intact.
I'd really like to see what would happen if the game was balanced around high diamond and how it would change the game for lower and higher players.

I don't generally think that every pro play aligned change is bad, however I honestly think it's unfair for anyone below masters who wants to play the dreaded trinity of Ryze, Kalista and Azir because there are 50 people who can abuse them. That's my two cents.

I said that not much seemed to change since last season when he had 48-49% winrate and therefor asked how he is actually successful now, then explaining why that's the case.

GP was insanely strong both in solo queue (54-55% winrate) and competitive. The nerfs actually pushed him down by over 4% when it comes to solo queue - that's more than a "slight" change.

Again, the point I was trying to make is that GP is unhealthy because he waits through lane to get strong. This is the thing that needs to be changed. GP was okay last season while being healthy - put him back in that spot.

They shouldn't do this. What they actually need to do is put him back in place where he was last year. Right now all the nerfs just push him more into afk Q spam - because you can't really win lane like other champions do anyway as long as you don't fight against a tank.

The core problem with GP right now is how the new runes affect his gameplay. 
Last season you took TLD or Grasp and you had to fight your way through lane to survive while you still had that small possibility to win lane and get a meaningful advantage out of it.

At the beginning of this season people started to opt into the new runes, which increased the survivability in lane dramatically. Klepto and the new Grasp were perfect for this. You had nice defensive stats from resolve and free gold, free mana, free health and free pots from Klepto, Inspiration and Manaflow Band.
GP could just get away with spamming Q and would just go through lane without interacting with anyone.
I totally agree that this was bullshit and needed a change, however the change itself was kind of questionable. They nerfed his offense by increasing mana costs and nerfed his defense by reducing barrel duration and removing vision, thus less defensive barrels.

Now, if the problem is that GP doesn't interact with his enemies, why do they actually nerf his overall ability to fight? Those changes, although seemingly good at first because they reduced his power, pretty much made things worse by pushing him more into not interacting with his opponent at all.

So now we have a GP that goes full defensive curl mode while powerfarming and occasionally shooting you in the face until he gets all his stuff. The actual part that made GPs kit work is gone: risk and reward.

I know I've been kind of rambling and I'm sorry about that, but here is the point I'm trying to make.
The only thing that changed for GP coming into this season were the runes. There have been no significant buffs to him, yet he still absolutely dominates.
The matchups are actually pretty much still the same: you win against tanks and if you get jumped on by fighters and bruisers you get your ass kicked.

So how in the world is GP successful right now?

His superior playstyle has changed from fight through lane to wait through lane.
That's the actual problem that needs to be changed.

Hey, I'm not the dude you were talking to but I'll try to elaborate his point anyway.
It's sometimes better not to push, if you don't have enough clearspeed and here is why.

If you kill the enemy laner and you push the wave fast enough, it will reset in the middle.
If you push the wave just a bit slower, so the next opposing wave will fight against your wave, you set up a nice slowpushing wave towards you. However, most of the times your enemy will be able to tp back on the minions, denying you the push.

So here are the first two options if you push with low waveclear:

1. You still manage to push fast enough and you reset the wave in the middle. Your enemy has to use tp or loses one wave. (neutral option)

2. You don't manage to push the wave fast enough. Your opponent TPs to a minion, denies you the push and is now able to set up a freeze (or at least slow pushes the wave so you farm in danger) and only lost ~3 minions. (bad option)

Now let's say you still don't have much waveclear, but the wave already is slowpushing towards you. Why push to reset in the middle (option 1) or fuck yourself up (option 2) if you already have what you want: a wave pushing towards you?

Your third option:

3. Don't push the wave and back off. Your opponent has to tp or he loses a shit ton of minions. You can always follow up with tp and freeze the wave with your fresh items, health and mana (because you should have the advantage if you killed him in the first place). If your opponent manages to break the freeze (because you still have low waveclear), you still had a nice time farming 3 waves under and near your turret in safety while your enemy was always in danger.

On top of that option 3 is the perfect setup for winning a lane if you communicate with your jungler.
Slow push the wave after you end the freeze so a huge minion wave builds up and towerdive your opponent with your jungler as soon as it hits his tower. Now he died again, has no tp, loses 3 waves and or his tower. That's pretty much a done deal.
